utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Will you please read the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-30/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Miroslav Kvocka, Mladjo Radic, Zoran Zigic, and Dragoljub Prcac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARMONA
utterances.text: Your Honour, my name is Anthony Carmona -- Your Honour, my name is Anthony Carmona and I appear on behalf of the Prosecution. Appearing with me for the Prosecution is Ms. Norul Rashid and Ms. Helen Brady. Ms. Lourdes Galicia is our case manager. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, my name is Krstan Simic and I appear for Miroslav Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, I am attorney Toma Fila and together with attorneys Zoran Jovanovic, I appear for Mladjo Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, I am attorney Slobodan Stojanovic, and I appear for Mr. Zoran Zigic. Thank you. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, I am Jovan Simic and I appear for Mr. Prcac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I want to ask the parties if there's anything they want to raise at this Status Conference. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARMONA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: I have one question to the Prosecution. And that is if there's still much material pending to disclose.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARMONA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can indicate that we have, in fact, completed our disclosure inquiry. And, in fact, as late as the 17th of September, approximately one month ago, we, in fact, disclosed some material to the Defence. I can indicate further that it is our habit that six months after a particular disclosure inquiry is done, we complete another. So that in the context of how we operate our modus, I can indicate to you that our next inquiry which would take place sometime in December. This is contingent of material being generated as a result of ongoing trials or as a result of investigations. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would it be too much to ask if the future disclosure that you just don't disclose the whole lump, but select what may be pertaining to the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARMONA
utterances.text: Certainly. It is our intention. We have, in fact, been doing that. Given the limited material that is coming forward, we are prepared to do the requisite review. In the context of relevance and in the context of the Rule 68 directive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Counsels. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no special issues to raise, but I must express my concern because of the length of these proceedings. Mr. Kvocka has been sentenced to seven years in prison. He has already been in detention for almost six years. And if these proceedings continue at this speed, I am afraid that he will have served his sentence before the documents are disclosed. We are rebutting the evidence in the file, not new evidence. So we wish to present our case as soon as possible and put an end to these lengthy proceedings, which I'm sure need not have taken so long. Unfortunately they have taken a long time and I am afraid that in these proceedings the right to an expeditious and fair trial has been imperilled and that has already been mentioned at the last Status Conference. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish to support what my colleague has said. If you look at the record of the last Status Conference, I said that the Prosecution is protracting these proceedings in the Krnojelac case. The judgment has been issued and I think there is no need any longer to waste time. Soon it will be two years from the decision of the Trial Chamber and this is actually a violation of human rights. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, certainly we are also in favour of a speedier resolution of this case, but we have to express our concern because three members of the Appeals Chamber have been changed, including the pre-Appeal Judge. We do not have any doubts about the abilities of the new Judges, and we are sure that they will fulfill everything that's required of them, but they will need time to familiarise themselves with this case, especially the case of Mr. Zigic. I feel that the case of Mr. Zigic is very complex. There are numerous counts, according to which he has been found guilty, numerous convictions, and we have appealed against these, which is why we feel that a thorough approach should be taken to the consideration of all these circumstances regardless of time. We do not require a decision which would be speedy, but based on erroneous facts. We are considering several new motions, including a motion based on Rule 115. We have a full understanding for the standpoints of other defence counsel who are in a hurry to have this appeal completed as soon as possible. And we would not object to this case being severed. We think this would make sense because Zigic has nothing in common with the others involved in the -- allegedly in the joint criminal enterprise. They are not accused of the same actions. So we would not oppose the case being severed. We feel that in this context, speed might be reflected in a poorer quality of proceedings, so we beg that all this be taken into account. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I do not think that speed and fairness are contradictory, and as far as I understand you have already two 115 motions presented. Do I understand from what you just said that you intend to present a third 115 motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have two motions, plus an additional motion. And we are considering yet another one. We feel that this has to do with some circumstances that have arisen since our appeal, so we feel that this would be timely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Well, in due time, the Bench will deal with your motion, if it is presented. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we agree with what our colleagues have said, but would like to add something. In our view, the Prosecution has a continuous obligation to disclose, and this is something that goes on. Otherwise, waiting for them to disclose everything at the rate at which they are doing it, we might find ourselves in a situation where they never disclose everything. If new material is discovered and they disclose it to us, we can then present our case to the Court. However, now, if you look at the records from the previous Status Conference, you will see that we have even waived our right to this material because we have an idea of what it might contain and the Defence has looked through most of this material during the trial itself. And we simply have been waiting for two years. Mr. Prcac is now in a poor state of health. During the trial we had health problems. Now he has been hospitalised for the third or fourth time, and his stays in hospital are growing longer and longer, and he's obviously under psychological pressure and is subject to psychosomatic complaints. So we are in a situation where we might fall ill because of the length of these proceedings. That is why we feel that Your Honour should set a deadline up to which the Prosecution should disclose everything they have. Please let us have a deadline for these review proceedings and then I really don't see Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. what the problem is and why we have to wait for them to disclose everything. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Yes. Does the Prosecution want to respond?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARMONA
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. I think my learned colleagues on the otherwise, with the exception of Mr. Simic, to some extent, do not fully appreciate the responsibilities of the Prosecution in relation to Rule 68. As indicated previously, Rule 68 material is not something that we essentially have sitting there. It may be something that is, in fact, generated from a trial where you have similar-type witnesses giving evidence. Apart from that, Your Honour will appreciate that ongoing investigations that may generate material that will essentially assist the Defence. So it is in their interest, as has been outlined and delineated by the previous Appeal Judge for the Prosecution to continue to vigorously, in fact, pursue its obligations in relation to Rule 68, and this is what we have done. We are not simply looking, sitting back. We are in fact -- if at any point of time there is material that comes to the fore, we make it available immediately. We say, for example, in our rule to be fair and just -- we say, for example, every six months we do such a review for that particular and specific purpose. Additionally, we are, in fact, quite anxious to expedite this appeal. But there is a process, and the process would inevitably incorporate potentially, if 115 material is accepted by the Chamber we, in fact, would have to in fact -- would have to file or adduce rebuttal evidence. So there is process. And it is a process that, in fact, that in no way we are attempting to stymie the expedition of the trial. We are anxious, as anxious, to expedite this matter. Additionally, I just wish to reiterate that this argument with regard for the need to severance was addressed previously by the pre-Appeal Judge and it was rejected. And we, in fact, continue to hold our ground on that issue, that this is a matter that should be heard in total with all the individual parties here in this court, being in a position for us to respond as is normal in a situation involving four accused persons. So to put it categorically: We oppose any request for severance because we think that the justice of this case holds that this matter be heard in its entirety with all the appellants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Anyway, it's not for the pre-Appeal Judge in a Status Conference to decide on this request for severance. I can only assure Mr. Zigic's counsel that even if there are new Judges on the bench, we are well acquainted with the case and that will not mean any delay. Is there any other matter the parties want to raise? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to dwell for a moment on this issue, because the Prosecutor was not present during the trial. The Kvocka Defence raised the issue of severance in July last year. However, this became moot because it appeared that the proceedings might be completed very soon. This was in July last year but now it's October and we are still on square one. I am touched by the Prosecution's concern for the interests of my client. I have to say, however, that the practice of this Tribunal has been that after having served two-thirds of their sentence, convicted persons have been released. On the 9th of December, 2002, my client served, so to speak, two-thirds of his sentence, and he's now nearing the end. Documents will keep turning up until 2010. Does this mean that my client has to wait for the year 2010 for us to be sure that the Prosecution wishes him well? That is why I suggest that as no decision was made regarding the issue of severance, because this question became moot, I propose that this be considered. We feel that there is no need for things that still have to be done to slow the proceedings for the other accused. Everything that has been done with regard to my client has actually been a waste of time. And it left the impression that this was really an obstruction of the proceedings, rather than an effort to be helpful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WEINBERG DE ROCA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic, and I understand you're the only one who did not present a 115 motion. If there's no other request for the floor, this conference will be adjourned. ---Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at 3.21 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25
